decision: Approved design: Password Strength Checker CLI, Test-First with Dataclass Output (Approach C over recommended Approach B). Three files: strength.py (PasswordResult dataclass + check() pure function), cli.py (thin entry point), test_strength.py (table-driven unit tests). Five rules exactly: length>=8, uppercase, lowercase, digit, special char (string.punctuation). Per-character unicode-aware checks for upper/lower (any(c.isupper() for c in password)), not whole-string. CLI stdin/stdout only, Python only, no external deps.

4-section review (architecture/code-quality/tests/performance): 2 issues found and resolved -- verify.py asserts by parsing 'Score: N/5' plus counting lines prefixed '- ' (can't access dataclass fields across a subprocess boundary), and a stdin-trailing-newline test case was added. Outside voice (Claude subagent fallback -- Codex auth expired and out of OpenRouter credits) surfaced 7 further spec gaps, all resolved directly: special-character detection is ASCII-only by design (string.punctuation) even though letter-case checks are unicode-aware -- this asymmetry is intentional, not an inconsistency; score is always computed as sum() of the five booleans inside check(), never independently settable; an empty string passed via argv[1] counts as a valid zero-length password (score 0/5), distinct from 'no input' (no argv + TTY stdin, exit 1); test_strength.py owns all rule/edge-case logic against the dataclass, verify.py owns only the CLI I/O contract (argv/stdin/TTY/exit codes/output parsing) via subprocess -- no duplication between the two. Verdict: CLEARED, 0 unresolved decisions, 0 critical failure-mode gaps. Sequential build, no parallelization opportunity (test_strength.py -> strength.py -> cli.py -> verify.py).
verify.py asserts score + reason-line count, not exact wording; score always-computed

Implemented strength.py, cli.py, test_strength.py, verify.py exactly per design doc and eng-review decisions -- no extra features or abstractions. python test_strength.py: 0 failures, exit 0. python verify.py: 7/7 checks passed, exit 0 (the 'no argv + TTY stdin' case is SKIPPED, not failed -- Windows has no stdlib pty module; platform gap already documented in the design doc's failure-modes table). Discovered mid-build: subprocess.DEVNULL reports isatty()==True in this Windows/Git-Bash environment, so the 'non-tty EOF' verify.py case uses an empty-string piped stdin instead of DEVNULL -- pipes are reliably non-tty across platforms, DEVNULL is not.

/code-review ran against the build diff (memory.json + 4 new files), confirmed correct via a full read plus running both test suites. 2 findings, both fixed: (1) memory.json's plan-eng-review timestamp was invented out of chronological order relative to later real-clock entries -- corrected to 2026-09-05T19:20:46, matching the actual eng-review-test-plan artifact's filename timestamp; (2) cli.py's manual `raw[:-1] if raw.endswith("\n") else raw` replaced with the equivalent, clearer stdlib `removesuffix("\n")`. Re-ran test_strength.py and verify.py after both fixes -- still exit 0 / 7/7 passed.

/qa's skill wasn't registered under ~/.claude/skills/qa (same gap hit earlier for plan-eng-review); copied it from ~/.claude/skills/gstack/qa. The skill itself is built around browser-driven web-app testing ($B/browse) with no CLI equivalent, so adapted it: exercised cli.py directly with 12 real-user and adversarial inputs (common weak password, shell-metacharacter password -- confirmed no injection since argv is never shell-interpreted, 10,000-char password for perf, CRLF stdin, emoji, blank-line stdin, multi-line stdin, invalid UTF-8 stdin, --help treated literally, both design-doc Success Criteria). 0 issues found, 0 fixes needed. Both design-doc success criteria confirmed. Report: .gstack/qa-reports/qa-report-password-strength-cli-2026-09-05.md

Full daily-mode audit (all 15 phases, 8/10 confidence gate). Attack surface is minimal by design: no network, no auth, no deps, no CI/CD, no persistence of the password anywhere. Secrets archaeology clean (git history + tracked files scanned, nothing found). Only one candidate finding surfaced: cli.py:9 accepts the password via argv (CWE-214, process-list/shell-history visibility). Independent verifier subagent scored it 3/10 -- not actionable for a single-user, no-persistence, no-multi-tenancy local CLI where stdin is already offered as the safer path -- so it was filtered by the confidence gate, not reported. Verdict: 0 findings. Non-security hygiene note (not a finding): .gstack/ is not yet in .gitignore, so local QA/security reports could get committed -- recommend adding it, did not fix since /cso is read-only by design. Report: .gstack/security-reports/2026-09-05-142846.json
